curated.otherUses: Approved for myelodysplastic syndromes, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and AML; a standard partner for venetoclax in older AML patients.

curated.otherUses: Investigated in advanced solid tumours; development discontinued.

curated.developer: Synthesised in 1959 at Upjohn, inspired by unusual nucleosides found in the Caribbean sponge Tectitethya crypta.
curated.mechanism: A cytosine analogue with the wrong sugar. Cells build it into DNA during replication, where it jams DNA polymerase and stalls the replication fork — so it kills whichever cells are dividing fastest.
curated.otherUses: The backbone of AML induction chemotherapy for fifty years; also used in acute lymphoblastic leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia in blast crisis, and lymphoma.

curated.otherUses: Investigated in renal cell carcinoma and other solid tumours; not approved.

curated.mechanism: A copper ionophore: it grabs copper ions and ferries them into mitochondria, where the metal overwhelms the cell with oxidative stress and triggers copper-dependent death. This is why it kills almost every sample in the panel — the mechanism is not specific to any mutation.
curated.otherUses: Failed a phase III trial in metastatic melanoma; now studied mainly as a copper-delivery tool and in copper-metabolism disease.

curated.mechanism: Selective inhibitor of spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK), a signalling hub downstream of immune receptors that some AML cells rely on.
curated.otherUses: Investigated in AML and B-cell malignancies; not approved.

Flavopiridol.family: CMGC: Containing CDK, MAPK, GSK3, CLK families

curated.mechanism: Inhibits cyclin-dependent kinases, especially CDK9. Blocking CDK9 stalls transcription, which rapidly depletes short-lived survival proteins such as MCL-1 that leukemia cells depend on.
curated.otherUses: Investigated in AML and chronic lymphocytic leukemia; not approved.

curated.otherUses: Investigated in gastric, papillary renal and head-and-neck cancers; not approved.

curated.mechanism: Pan-class-I PI3K inhibitor, blocking the pathway that relays growth-factor signals to AKT.
curated.otherUses: Investigated in breast and lung cancer; not approved.

curated.mechanism: Binds the protein FKBP12; that pair then clamps mTORC1, shutting down the growth-and-protein-synthesis programme cells run when nutrients are plentiful.
curated.otherUses: Approved as sirolimus to prevent kidney transplant rejection, and for lymphangioleiomyomatosis; also used on drug-eluting coronary stents.

curated.mechanism: Binds the ATP pocket shared by almost every protein kinase, so it inhibits hundreds of them at once. That total lack of selectivity is exactly why it is used: it is the positive control that should kill any sample.
curated.otherUses: Far too toxic to be a medicine. Its chemistry was the starting point for midostaurin.

Vargetef.family: Type IV RTKs: VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) receptor family

curated.developer: Boehringer Ingelheim. This is nintedanib, sold as Vargatef and Ofev.
curated.mechanism: A triple angiokinase inhibitor blocking VEGFR, FGFR and PDGFR simultaneously, cutting off three separate routes tumours use to recruit blood vessels.
curated.otherUses: Approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other progressive fibrosing interstitial lung diseases, and in the EU with docetaxel for advanced non-small-cell lung adenocarcinoma.

Vatalanib (PTK787).family: Type IV RTKs: VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) receptor family

curated.developer: AbbVie (from Abbott's BCL-2 programme) with Genentech/Roche; originally ABT-199.
curated.mechanism: A BH3-mimetic: it plugs the groove on the BCL-2 protein that normally sequesters pro-death partners. Freed, those partners trigger apoptosis, so the leukemia cell executes the self-destruct programme it had been suppressing.
curated.otherUses: Approved for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma, and for AML in combination with azacitidine, decitabine or low-dose cytarabine in adults unfit for intensive chemotherapy.

curated.mechanism: Inhibits polo-like kinase 1, a master regulator of mitotic entry and exit, arresting dividing cells and driving them to apoptosis.
curated.otherUses: Investigated in AML, including in older patients with cytarabine; not approved.
